articles.summary:
Maputo 5th August: The regional specialist financial sector development agency, FSD Africa, funded by the UK Government, launched a new programme to finance small and growing businesses across Mozambique. The programme name “RAIZ” (Resilience, Adaptation, and Innovation in Mozambique – “root” in Portuguese) underlines its emphasis on rooting alternative financing options for small and growing businesses in the country in partnership with capital providers, investors and other stakeholders.

articles.title: Austria announces energy storage offensive, shifting solar subsidy focus
articles.summary:
The debate over the design of Austria’s subsidy framework has intensified since the last funding round, which saw its budget exhausted in just 33 seconds. Thousands of applications for photovoltaic and battery storage investment grants were left unfunded. A female small business owner and customer of one of our financed portfolio companies in Burkina Faso, Oolu by Ignite, can now contribute to the household economy thanks to an installed off-grid solar kit that provides electricity for running a refrigerator.

In a neighbourhood of Bobo-Dioulasso, where grid infrastructure exists but electricity has yet to arrive, Tinta Setou and her family used to rely on charcoal, gas and small solar lamps for their daily energy needs. The lamps provided only a few hours of light each night, limiting household activities and business opportunities.

articles.title: Mid-term evaluation confirms BGFA programme is on track and delivering results
articles.summary:
An independent mid-term evaluation of the Beyond the Grid Fund for Africa (BGFA) confirms that the programme is delivering strong results in expanding access to off-grid clean energy in Sub-Saharan Africa.

The evaluation, carried out by Oxford Policy Management, confirms that BGFA is on the right track to reach its programme target of establishing 1.7 million new energy service subscriptions by 2028 across five countries; Burkina Faso, the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), Liberia, Uganda and Zambia. The evaluation also highlights that the programme has generated valuable insights and lessons for the sector and for future results-based financing programmes supporting the scale-up of clean energy.

articles.title: Ghana advances Mission 300 reforms with a $4.4bn energy investment pipeline behind them
articles.summary:
Accra has moved on the commitments in its national energy compact, and the African Development Bank now describes a pipeline of that scale gathering behind the reforms. The sequencing matters more than the total, because compact reforms are what convert a pipeline into projects that reach financial close.

Ghana advanced its Mission 300 reform commitments through July, with the African Development Bank describing a US$4.4 billion energy investment pipeline gaining momentum behind them.
